# Ralph Progress Journal - MOSS live meeting transcription MVP

Append-only. Agents add one entry per iteration; the launcher adds one-line
"[loop <run-id>] ..." markers at run boundaries. Never rewrite or delete
entries — context.md is the place for current state, this file is history.

Entry format (concise, a few lines each):

  ## Iteration <n> - <short focus>
  - Target: <candidate from context.md, or off-list + justification>
  - Files: <paths>
  - Validation: <command> -> <result>
  - Evidence: <artifact/log paths>
  - Learned: <what changed in understanding>
  - Next: <recommended next step>

Started: 2026-07-27 - Branch `ralph/live-meeting-mvp` cut from `main af3ac36` (clean tree). The
loop executes revision 3 of
`/Users/gao/Desktop/AI_Projects/0.AISIGHT_LOOP/moss-transcribe-diarize/docs/live-capture-gap-and-execution-plan-20260727.md`.
Feasibility is settled by measurement, not assumption: MOSS decodes a 7.5 s span in 0.233 s
(RTF 0.031) on the already-resident 4070Ti vLLM engine, so live transcription needs no extra VRAM
and latency is governed by the endpoint span cap alone. Seven defects are confirmed with
file:line anchors (pairing contract, no pinning, destructive frame drain, 900 s viewer expiry,
sequential blocking POSTs, mismatched keychain access group, no client-side 16 kHz conversion);
two of them are already fixed on `acl/IDEA-044--A-034@67a27b8` and are to be grafted rather than
rewritten. The server runs `163e969` with live disabled and 84 unpushed commits behind local
`main`; the MacBook has no installed app and its checkout points at OpenMOSS upstream. Mac code
signing is solved by a scripted self-signed identity in a dedicated keychain (proven over SSH,
designated requirement stable across rebuilds); the login keychain is locked to SSH sessions, so
neither the existing `LiveTranscribe Local Dev` identity nor the Keychain secret store can be used
non-interactively. The only irreducible human step is two TCC clicks on m4mbp — park and report
there. This loop is the single writer on this repo; the governed aisight-coding-loop stays halted.

## Iteration 2 - explicit per-lane permission coordinator (A3)
- Target: Phase A candidate A3 — close defect 9 with generation-fenced pending/granted/denied
  per-lane permission transitions and a typed denied-lane failure
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/{MicrophoneCapture,SystemAudioTap,
  NativeDualCaptureSource}.swift`; `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/MOSSCaptureCoreTests/
  CaptureControllerTests.swift`; `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`
- Method: locality-constrained by design. `spikes/idea-044-attempt2-red-control/repro.py` fixes
  the registered thirteen paths, so the coordinator could not be a new file: it lives in
  `NativeDualCaptureSource.swift` as `NativeLanePermissionCoordinator`, the explicit microphone
  transition in `MicrophoneCapture.swift`, and the system-lane rule in `SystemAudioTap.swift` as
  `SystemAudioPermission`. Behaviour: `MicrophoneCapture.start` now requires `.granted` before it
  touches `AVAudioEngine.inputNode`; an `.undetermined` lane gets one
  `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .audio)` and stays `pending`; the source runs when at least
  one lane is capturing and a pending lane joins later on a grant; when nothing is capturing,
  `start` retires the permission generation and throws the pending lane's typed
  `permissionDenied`; `stop` retires before teardown; a duplicate `start` adopts the running
  generation and never prompts twice.
- Validation:
  - `swift build --product MOSSCaptureApp` -> OK; `--product mtd-capture` -> OK
  - `swift test --package-path macos/MOSSCapture` -> **92 passed, 0 failures** (was 81)
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py -q
    -p no:cacheprovider` -> **2 passed in 9.22 s** (was 1 passed / 1 failed on an 8 s
    `TimeoutExpired`). The real built app now answers `start`, `stop` and `status` on an ungranted
    host; `start` takes the tracer's typed-failure branch, so no lane is ever falsely reported as
    recording
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **456 passed,
    2 skipped, 346 subtests** (454+2, no regression)
  - `spikes/idea-044-attempt2-red-control/repro.py --target "$PWD"` -> **5/10** (was 1/10); all
    five permission checks green
  - `bash scripts/ralph-afk/validate-phase-a-locality.sh` -> PASS; `git diff --check` -> clean
- Evidence: discriminator output above; new Swift nodes
  `testDuplicateStartDoesNotRequestPermissionsTwice`,
  `testStopDuringPermissionPromptCancelsGeneration`,
  `testLatePermissionCompletionAfterStopIsNoop`,
  `testStartWithNoLaneRecordingReportsThePendingPermissionAndDisownsIt`,
  `testUndeterminedMicrophonePromptsOnceAndJoinsRunningCaptureOnGrant`,
  `testUndeterminedMicrophoneDenialFailsOnlyThatLane`,
  `test{System,Microphone}GrantedWith{Microphone,System}DeniedKeepsLanePermissionsIndependent`,
  `testMicrophoneCaptureUndeterminedPermissionNeverTouchesInputNode`,
  `testSystemAudioPermissionIsResolvedByTheUserInitiatedRecordingStart`,
  `testLanePermissionCoordinatorKeepsLaneStateAndFencesRetiredAnswers`
- Learned: (1) the attempt-2 red control is the real design spec, not just a gate — it fixes both
  the file locality and the type names (`PermissionCoordinator` in the dual source,
  `SystemAudioPermission`/`requestSystemAudio` in the tap, `requestAccess`+`.audio` in the
  microphone), so read it before designing any Phase-A change. (2) Retiring the *health*
  generation on a failed `start` destroys the per-lane failure evidence `status` must report;
  only the permission generation may be retired there. Caught by
  `testNativeDualCaptureSourceUnwindsBothLanesWhenEveryStartFails`. (3) `CaptureLane` is a public
  enum, so Swift does not infer `Sendable`; carrying a lane into an asynchronous permission answer
  needs the explicit conformance.
- Blocker: none. Known open risk recorded in context.md: `AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap` is still
  called on the control thread. It returns promptly on MacStudio (iteration-1 `sample` located the
  hang in the microphone path), but M36 is only fully answered once m4mbp shows it also returns
  while its own TCC prompt is on screen.
- Next: A2 — move `handoff` into the app dispatcher and strip view-token/pasteboard authority from
  the CLI (discriminator checks 1-4), then the tracer evidence for check 10, then A4.

## Iteration 3 - app-owned UDS handoff (A2)
- Target: Phase A candidate A2 — move view authority and the pasteboard write out of the CLI and
  into the app dispatcher (discriminator checks 1-4)
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/{CaptureSecurity,CaptureCommandLine}.swift`,
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/{MOSSCaptureApp,MTDCaptureCLI}/main.swift`,
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/{MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift,
  MTDCaptureCLITests/MTDCaptureCLITests.swift}`; `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`
- Method: `CapturePortalHandoffConfirmation` / `CapturePortalHandoffAdapter` /
  `PasteboardCapturePortalHandoff` moved from `CaptureCommandLine.swift` to `CaptureSecurity.swift`
  (a registered path, and where the dispatcher that now owns them lives); the confirmation stopped
  being its own Codable wire type and became a plain value the dispatcher maps onto a new
  `ControlChannelResponse.viewAuthority` field, so the CLI relays one response type for every
  command. `ControlCommandDispatcher` gained an optional `portalHandoff` and `case "handoff"`;
  `MOSSCaptureApp/main.swift` is the only injector. The CLI's two-round-trip
  `status`-then-local-handoff path is gone: it now sends one
  `ControlChannelRequest(command: "handoff")`. `CaptureCLIError` lost
  `portalHandoffUnavailable`/`pasteboardUnavailable`; those are now `CaptureSecurityError` cases,
  so `sanitizedControlError` names them without leaking anything.
- Validation:

  - `swift test --package-path macos/MOSSCapture` -> **95 passed, 0 failures** (was 92)

    -p no:cacheprovider` -> **2 passed in 8.48 s**. This is the real evidence: the tracer runs the
    *built* CLI's `handoff` against the *built* app over real same-user UDS, asserts the exact body

    asserts no secret appears in CLI output, and `_assert_named_pasteboard_matches_store` still

  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **456 passed,

- Method: the tracer's only fixed path is now
  `macos/MOSSCapture/.build/idea044-lab/MOSSCapture.app`, held under an exclusive `flock` on a
  sibling `install.lock` for the whole pytest process (acquired once, released on exit, bounded

  `MOSSCaptureApp`, writes the product `Info.plist` verbatim — identifier
  `com.alphasight.moss.capture` plus both `NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription` and
  `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, asserted non-empty at install — ad-hoc signs the bundle, then

  per-file inventory hashes, `executable_sha256`, `bundle_sha256`, the `codesign -d -r -`
  designated requirement, and provenance `built_product {macho_uuid, sha256}`. Reinstall happens
  only when the built product's Mach-O UUID or sha256 moves. Every later node calls
  `_assert_lab_bundle_unchanged`, which re-observes the bundle from disk and demands byte-equality
  with the recorded evidence plus `codesign --verify --strict`. The lab node additionally re-enters
  the install path and asserts the evidence file's own inode, mtime_ns and bytes are unmoved — the
  direct answer to "rebuilding at the same path and bundle ID is not continuity proof". Certificate,
  server, port, UDS, secret store and artifacts stay per-test temporary; `_make_temp_app_bundle` is
  deleted. `_swift_bin_dir()` is memoized so the three call sites do not re-shell `swift build`.

## Iteration 5 - production file secret store is the default (B1)
- Target: Phase B candidate B1. Make `FileCaptureSecretStore` the default for both products at
  `~/Library/Application Support/MOSSCapture/secrets.json` (0700 dir, 0600 file, atomic
  replacement, one path shared by app and CLI) and strip the mismatched Keychain access group.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/CaptureSecurity.swift`;
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/{MOSSCaptureApp,MTDCaptureCLI}/main.swift`;
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/{MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift,
  MTDCaptureCLITests/MTDCaptureCLITests.swift}`; `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`
- Method: `CaptureSecretStoreSelection` gained `defaultPath(homeDirectory:)` and lost the
  `keychainDefault:` autoclosure; `makeDefault` now always returns a `FileCaptureSecretStore`,
  taking a non-empty `MOSS_CAPTURE_SECRET_STORE_PATH` as an override. Both composition roots call
  `CaptureSecretStoreSelection.makeDefault()` with no arguments, so the env-key literal and the
  path rule have exactly one owner and the two products cannot drift apart. `KeychainCaptureSecretStore`
  keeps its `SecItem*` implementation but lost `accessGroup` entirely (a shared group needs a Team
  ID a locally signed identity does not have) and is now documented as dormant. `FileCaptureSecretStore`
  gained a `path` accessor and a `prepareDirectory()` that creates the directory 0700, tightens a

## Iteration 6 - retained-until-ACK outbox (B2)
- Target: Phase B candidate B2 / plan D5. Kill defect 3 (frame loss on any transient send
  failure): retain 15 s of audio per lane keyed by `(lane, sequence)`, retry the identical frame on
  timeout/429/ambiguous answers, release only on an acknowledgement, and surface a typed degraded
  state on overflow.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/CaptureOutbox.swift` (new);
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/{CaptureController,CaptureSecurity}.swift`;
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift`;
  `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`
- Method: `CaptureFrameOutbox` sits between `source.pendingFrames()` and `transport.publish` and
  owns **wire identity** — it stamps the `(lane, sequence)` a frame keeps for every attempt. That is
  what makes overflow survivable: the outbox **refuses** new audio when a lane is full instead of
  evicting a retained frame, and because a refused frame burns no sequence number the admitted
  stream stays gapless, so the lane keeps publishing instead of being rejected forever as out of
  order (`live_ingest.py:_check_epoch`/sequence check would 409 every later frame). Capacity is
  measured in audio seconds from each frame's own `sampleCount / sampleRate`, not in frames, so
  B3's frame-size/rate change needs no edit here. Loss is reported three ways: `refusedFrames`, a
  sticky `degradation` (`overflowedLaneRetention` / `undeliverableFrame`, never cleared by later
  success), and `discontinuity = true` on the next frame that lane admits. `reset()` runs on every
  `start` because a server session numbers each lane from zero. `publishPendingFrames` now admits
  everything first, then flushes in global admission order, stalling only the failing lane;
  `CaptureFrameRetryPolicy` is the one classifier (0/408 ambiguous, 429 backpressure, 5xx
  serverUnavailable, transient `URLError` ambiguous; 4xx / missing bearer / missing pin /
  `secureConnectionFailed` / `cancelled` not retryable). Depth and degradation reach the operator
  through `CaptureStatus.outbox` and `ControlChannelResponse.outboxRetainedFrames` /
  `.outboxDegradation`; the `moss-live-helper-health.v1` heartbeat wire was left alone.
  Two adjacent defects surfaced while writing the ambiguous-answer node and were closed with it:
  (a) a publish throw inside `start` failed the start while `state.beginStart` had already set
  `running = true` and no pump task existed — a zombie capture that could never publish or be
  restarted; a retryable failure is now a degraded start (pump scheduled, audio retained) and an
  unretryable one stops the source and rolls the state back; (b) a raw `URLError` — exactly what
  the pinned `URLSession` throws during a real outage — typed as `CapturePumpFailure.unexpected`
  instead of `.transportUnavailable`.

  - `pytest tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **3 passed in 6.73s**

- Learned: (1) the outbox has to own the wire sequence, otherwise refusing a frame on overflow
  burns a number the emitter already assigned and the server rejects every subsequent frame of that
  lane as out of order — a bounded queue would have converted a transient overload into a dead lane.

  publish attempt best-effort by construction, which exposed the pre-existing zombie-start path:
  once audio is never lost, failing the whole start on a network hiccup is strictly wrong.
  (4) Sticky degradation is the only honest reading of "never report clean" — an overflow that later
  drains still lost audio, so `degradation` survives recovery and resets only on a new session.

## Iteration 7 - canonical 16 kHz wire format and converted-nanosecond timestamps (B3)
- Target: Phase B candidate B3 / plan D13 + D14. Kill defects 7 and 8: both lanes must leave the
  Mac as 16 kHz mono in exact 8000-sample frames, and `capture_timestamp_ns` must be real
  nanoseconds in one Mac host-time domain rather than raw Mach ticks.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/NativeLaneWireFormat.swift` (new);
  `.../{NativeAudioBuffers,NativeDualCaptureSource,CaptureController,MicrophoneCapture,
  SystemAudioTap}.swift`; `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift`;
  `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`
- Method: everything unsafe on a Core Audio callback thread moved into one new file and one caller.
  `NativeLaneWireStream` (per lane) converts host ticks to nanoseconds, downmixes to mono,
  resamples through one stateful `AVAudioConverter`, and coalesces exact 8000-sample frames;
  `NativeLaneFrameEmitter` sequences and encodes what comes out. The drivers still only copy and
  enqueue, and they now hand over zero ticks when `AVAudioTime.isHostTimeValid` /
  `AudioTimeStamp.mFlags.hostTimeValid` is absent, which the conversion stage refuses.
  Two design choices carried the iteration. (1) Frame timestamps are re-derived from every
  buffer's own converted capture instant (`pendingStartNS = capturedNS - duration(pending)`)
  instead of accumulated as `anchor + n x 500 ms`: cadence-accumulated stamps would drift away
  from the host clock by the audio-device clock error over a meeting-length run, and the Phase F
  latency number is measured against exactly that clock. Cost: <= 1 wire sample of cadence jitter
  plus a fixed converter group delay, both measured below. (2) The outbox's capacity is in audio
  seconds, so the frame-size and rate change needed no edit there - 15 s per lane is now 30 frames
  instead of a rate-dependent count.
  A frame is emitted only at full size; the trailing partial leaves through `flush()`, which
  `NativeDualCaptureSource.stop` calls before parking the tail for one final `pendingFrames()`,
  and `CaptureController.stop` now drains once after stopping the source so the tail actually
  reaches the wire instead of being dropped at the end of every meeting.

## Iteration 8 - bounded concurrent transport (B4)
- Target: Phase B candidate B4 / defect 5. Bound what the transport can have outstanding, in width
  (requests) and in time (overlapping passes), and stop building a TLS session per frame.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/CapturePublishPump.swift` (new);
  `.../{CaptureController,CaptureHTTPTransport,CaptureScheduling,FakeCaptureAdapters}.swift`;
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureApp/main.swift`;
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift`;
  `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`
- Method: four changes, one contract.
  (1) `CaptureFramePublishPump` is now the only caller of `transport.publish`. One pre-created
      serial `DispatchQueue` per lane: a lane has at most one request in flight because its stream
      must arrive in sequence order, and the lanes run at the same time because nothing couples
      them. In-flight work is `CaptureLane.allCases.count` and does not grow with the backlog, the
      meeting length or the tick count. B2's one-head-retry-per-lane-per-tick rule is unchanged;
      the reported failure is now picked in lane order so a two-lane outage is deterministic.
  (2) Passes never overlap. `Contention.skip` for the periodic tick (its audio is already retained;
      a second pass over the same frames would publish identities that are in flight and multiply
      in-flight work by the number of late ticks) and `.wait` for start and stop (the meeting's
      final frames reach the wire only through the stop's pass). A skipped tick still emits health
      — a long recovery drain must not read as a dead helper against the 30 s lease.
  (3) The app's pump interval was a `0.25` literal; it is now `CapturePumpContract.interval` = 0.5 s,
      the prd's domain value and exactly one canonical wire frame per lane per tick.
  (4) `PinnedURLSessionCaptureHTTPClientProvider` caches one client per pin and `invalidate()`s a
      superseded one. Before this, `publish` called the provider per frame and the provider built a
      fresh ephemeral `URLSession` every time: a TLS handshake per 0.5 s of audio per lane, and —
      because a session retains its delegate until invalidated — a leaked session plus pinning
      delegate per frame for the whole meeting (~14,400 in a 60-minute two-lane run). The app now
      builds one provider and hands it to frames, heartbeat and pairing.

  - `pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **457 passed, 2 skipped, 346 subtests** (unchanged)
  - `spikes/idea-044-attempt2-red-control/repro.py --target "$PWD"` -> **10/10**, unchanged
  - `leak-scan.sh` -> `leak-scan: clean`; `git diff --check` -> clean

    reads it after `beginPass`. Admission from the source stays outside the turn on purpose — a
    skipped tick must still drain the source's bounded ring into the outbox, which is where loss is

    never published (`[1]` not `[1, 2]`), `publishedFrameCount` 0 and `outbox.retainedFrames` 2 —

    requests instead of 1. Reverted -> green, 121 passed.
- Learned: (1) The re-entry guard and the frame snapshot are one decision, not two. Winning the turn
  is worthless if the caller already decided what to send — a waiting stop with a stale list is
  exactly the duplicate publisher the guard was added to prevent. (2) A per-request `URLSession` is
  invisible in tests and unbounded in production: nothing fails, the process just accumulates one
  session and one strongly-retained pinning delegate per frame. Making the provider's construction
  count observable is what turned it into a node. (3) Concurrency can be proven without sleeping by
  making the fake refuse to proceed until the concurrency actually exists; the serial implementation
  then fails on a deadline, which is a real signal rather than a slow-machine artifact. (4) Giving
  up cross-lane publish order is the price of lane concurrency, and it was cheap only because the
  wire contract is per-lane; the tests that asserted global order were asserting an implementation
  detail.

  - **The status a viewer must follow is not `session.status`.** Written as a status-only check the
    failed-stop node returned `'active' != 'failed'`: a runtime terminal failure (stop that fails
    accounting, helper lease expiry) refuses every later frame while the mono session still reads
    `active`. `_session_status` now reports `failed` whenever `snapshot.terminal_failure is not
    None`. Found by the test, not by review, and it is exactly the case a mirror cannot cover -
    the failed-stop path releases v2/mixer/presence but deliberately **not** the access entry,
    because the capture client still has to be able to abort and clean up (existing

  - Fail-closed is structural: an unwired registry grants **no** view authority, so authority that

    API surface is guarded by an exact set, so the route was added there deliberately.
- Learned: (1) "Bound to the session lifecycle" is only real if the authority *asks* the lifecycle
  owner; a copy maintained by four call sites is a mirror, and the hole is always the error path
  that forgot to update it. (2) Two terminal representations coexist here - `session.status` and
  `terminal_failure` - and the ownership entry has a third lifetime again, because capture needs to
  outlive the session's death long enough to abort. Keeping those three separate is what let the
  view die immediately without stranding the capture client. (3) The one thing to re-check at F3:
  the 16-minute soak now depends on `closing` being viewable, so a viewer polling through a drain
  keeps working and only the terminal transition cuts it off.

## Iteration 12 (run 20260728-023004-98501, its iteration 4) - generated manifest bounds (C2)
- Target: Phase C candidate C2. B3 made the Mac client send exact 8000-sample 16 kHz frames, but
  the bounds the server admits them against live in the *host* manifest, which nothing in the repo
  generated or checked. The deployed provisional still carried the 7.5 s span cap and 30 s
  retention, so a >15-minute meeting would have been admitted against pre-retune bounds.
- Files: `moss_transcribe_diarize/app/live_manifest_finalizer.py` (new),
  `ops/finalize-live-provider-manifest.py` (new, tracked wrapper),
  `tests/test_live_manifest_finalizer.py` (new), `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`.
  No existing product source changed.
- Method: make the bounds **generated, with every relation checked**, rather than typed into a
  JSON file. The three tuned bounds are required flags (the plan's latency remedy tunes the span
  cap 40000 -> 32000 -> 24000, so they cannot be constants), and everything else is a derived
  relation the tool refuses to violate. Hashes are regenerated from the retuned sections; admission
  is then proven with the runtime's own readers (`_endpoint_config`, `_bounds`,
  `LiveServiceDescriptor`) before anything is written. Output discipline copied from B5's
  `moss-tool-lib.sh`: dry-run plan, rollback line before the first mutation, `unchanged:` re-run,
  backup instead of delete, `evidence: key=value`.
- Validation:
  - `pytest tests/test_live_manifest_finalizer.py -q` -> **17 passed**
  - `pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **492 passed, 2 skipped, 368 subtests** in 40.0s
    (was 475/2/368; +17 nodes, no regressions)
  - `spikes/idea-044-attempt2-red-control/repro.py --target "$PWD"` -> **10/10**, unchanged
  - `leak-scan.sh` -> `leak-scan: clean`
  - Swift untouched this iteration (no Swift source changed); last measured 121 passed at
    iteration 11.
- Evidence:
  - **The real host input was measured before trusting the tool** (read-only ssh probe, nothing
    mutated): the staged provisional carries `frame_samples 4000`, `hard_cap_samples 120000` in
    *both* `endpoint_config` and `bounds_config`, `max_retained_samples 480000`,
    `max_frame_samples 16000`, `decoder max_samples 120000`, `min_silence_samples 8000`, paddings
    1600, `source_revision "PROVISIONAL-UPDATE-AFTER-KEEPER"`. So every field the finalizer does
    not set already satisfies the contract and D2 will not be refused - and the test fixture now
    mirrors those exact values instead of invented ones.
  - The two hard caps are separate fields with separate readers: `EndpointPolicy` closes the span
    and `LiveSession` freezes it. The host file happens to hold them equal; nothing enforced it.
    The tool now sets both from one flag and refuses a divergence, because a smaller freeze cap
    would split spans the endpoint had not closed.
  - Capacity headroom is measured, not asserted in prose: a `LiveLaneIngress` at the generated
    960000 accepts one 2.5 s span plus a full 15 s reconnect burst on **both** lanes
    (35 frames/lane = 280000 samples), the oldest burst frame still replays to the identical ack
    (70 acks used of the shared 256-entry window), the lane fills to exactly 120 frames = 60.0 s,
    and frame 121 raises `LiveV2LaneCapacityError`.
  - Mutation rehearsal 1 (drop the `max_retained_samples` assignment): 5 nodes fail, including the
    capacity-headroom node and the ops-tool end-to-end node. Reverted -> green.
  - Mutation rehearsal 2 (inherit `config_hashes` from the input instead of regenerating): **7**

  - Mutation rehearsal 4 (drop `hard_cap_samples <= decoder_config.max_samples`): the

  - Refusals cover: the `PROVISIONAL-...` placeholder, an uppercase SHA, a short SHA, a 4000-sample
    frame, a cap that is not a whole wire frame, a cap below `min_silence_samples`, a cap beyond the

- Learned: (1) The plan's ordered latency remedy (2.0 s span cap) is why the bounds cannot be
  constants in the server - but the *relations* can be, and the relations are what a wrong flag
  violates. Required flags plus checked relations gave both. (2) Verifying admission inside the
  generator - with the runtime's readers, before writing - turned "the tests check the tool" into

  (3) Probing the real host input first was worth more than any local fixture: it proved the two

## Iteration 13 (run 20260728-023004-98501, its iteration 5) - live TLS material + loopback pairing (C3a)
- Target: Phase C candidate C3, split as iteration 12 recommended. This iteration is C3a - the two
  *credential* tools D2 and D4 run on the host: `ops/generate-live-tls.sh` and `ops/live-pair.sh`.
  They are one logical change because they are coupled by one value: SHA-256 over the leaf
  certificate's DER bytes. The generator mints it, the server derives it from the same file
  (`web_cli._certificate_sha256`) and stamps it into every pairing payload, and the Mac compares it
  to the leaf a handshake offers (`FullCertificatePinValidator`, 64 lowercase hex, nothing else).
  The staged host material has no tailnet SAN (plan D9), so nothing in the repo could generate the
  certificate the browser has to match, and nothing could mint a payload on the loopback-only route.
- Files: `ops/moss-ops-lib.sh` (new), `ops/generate-live-tls.sh` (new), `ops/live-pair.sh` (new),
  `tests/test_live_deployment_credentials.py` (new), `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`.
  **No product source changed** (`git diff --name-only` touches only ops/, tests/ and the loop dir).
- Method: names are flags with checked relations, exactly C2's shape - a deployment states its own
  DNS names and addresses, and an address is refused unless it is inside the networks `live_auth`
  admits, so the tool cannot mint material for a peer the server itself would reject. What was
  passed in is an input; what the generated file says is evidence (SAN set, `serverAuth`,
  key/certificate pairing, and the pin computed two independent ways which must agree) and the
  installed file is re-read again after the move. Output discipline is B5's, via a Linux-side
  `moss-ops-lib.sh`; the two libraries stay separate because the primitives differ per host family
  and a parity node compares their emitted lines byte for byte.
- Validation:
  - `pytest tests/test_live_deployment_credentials.py -q` -> **14 passed** in 10.7s
  - `pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **506 passed, 2 skipped, 368 subtests** in 49.5s
    (was 492/2/368; +14 nodes, no regressions)
  - `spikes/idea-044-attempt2-red-control/repro.py --target "$PWD"` -> **10/10**, unchanged
  - `leak-scan.sh` -> `leak-scan: clean`; `git diff --check` -> clean
  - `bash -n` on all three new scripts -> clean; every script is bash-3.2 compatible (MacStudio's
    /bin/bash is 3.2.57, the server's is 5.x, so 3.2 is the binding constraint - no associative
    arrays, no `${var,,}`, `[[ =~ ]]` and `$'\n'` verified by hand under 3.2 before use)
  - Swift untouched this iteration (no Swift source changed); last measured 121 passed at
    iteration 11.
- Evidence:
  - **The pin is proven identical across four readers**: the tool's `evidence: pin=`, the server's
    own `web_cli._certificate_sha256`, `hashlib.sha256(ssl.PEM_cert_to_DER_cert(...))` computed in
    the test without either implementation, and the leaf a *real handshake* offers - the node loads
    the generated pair into an `SSLContext` (the same `load_cert_chain` call uvicorn makes) and
    reads the certificate back with `ssl.get_server_certificate`. A key that did not belong to the
    certificate would fail at `load_cert_chain`, so that node covers the pairing too.
  - **A re-run must not rotate.** This started as tidiness and turned out to be the safety property
    of the tool: the pin is what every paired Mac stores, so an accidental second run would break a
    live client with a pin mismatch and invalidate every outstanding payload. A re-run with the same
    names in a different order and a different `--days` prints `unchanged:`, emits no `change:` line
    and leaves inode, mtime and bytes untouched. Rotation is `--rotate` only, and a name change, CN
    change, near-expiry or half-installed pair is *refused* with the exact re-run command rather
    than silently rotated.
  - **`live-pair.sh` catches the rotated-but-not-restarted service.** The payload carries the digest
    of the certificate the *running process* loaded; the tool compares it with the digest of the
    file on disk and refuses to print anything when they differ, naming both digests. Without this
    the failure mode surfaces on the Mac as an unexplained pinning failure with a valid-looking
    pairing code. Proven with a real uvicorn TLS server on cert A and `--cert` pointing at cert B.
  - Secret hygiene is measured, not asserted in prose: two real payloads are minted from the real
    `POST /api/live/pairing-codes` route over real TLS, each printed exactly once on its own
    `payload:` line, and the node then walks the whole tree under the tool's HOME, TMPDIR and
    working directory and asserts neither secret reached any file - plus not stderr, not an
    `evidence:` value, and not the server's persisted auth state. The two mints differ, so nothing
    is cached or replayed.
  - Address admission is a **parity table against the server**, asked through `LiveAccessRegistry`'s
    public surface rather than by copying its network tuple: 14 IPv4 cases including the exact
    boundaries 100.63.255.255/100.64.0.8/100.128.0.1 and 172.15/172.16/172.32, plus 169.254.1.1,
    8.8.8.8 and two malformed values. The tool's accept/refuse agrees with the server on all 14.
    IPv6 is refused although the server admits ULA and link-local: narrower than the server is safe,
    wider would not be, and that direction is asserted.
  - A dry run validates *before* it plans: 15 malformed-input cases produce zero `plan:` lines, so
    `--dry-run` refuses exactly what a real run would. A failed generation (openssl stubbed to fail
    at `req`) leaves no certificate, no key and an empty scratch TMPDIR.
  - Mutation rehearsal 1 (drop the payload-vs-disk digest cross-check): the mismatch node fails.
    Reverted -> green.
  - Mutation rehearsal 2 (also emit the payload as an `evidence:` line): the secrecy node fails.
    Reverted -> green.
  - Mutation rehearsal 3 (make the `unchanged:` branch unreachable, i.e. rotate on every run): the
    no-rotate node fails. Reverted -> green.
  - Mutation rehearsal 4 (print `rollback:` after the moves instead of before): the reversible-
    rotation node fails on ordering. Reverted -> green.
  - Mutation rehearsal 5 (drop the loopback check in `live-pair.sh`): the pre-send node fails - and
    it fails *by reaching the stub curl*, which is what the marker file in that node is for.
  - Found while writing it: `10.0.0.5` is a label-legal DNS name, so an address typed into `--dns`
    was accepted and would have become a DNS-type name that matches nothing. Fixed generally - a
    final label that is all digits is not a hostname - so `8.8.8.8` is caught the same way, and the
    error says which flag to use.
  - Not covered here on purpose: exchanging a minted payload needs a non-loopback TLS peer, which
    `tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py` already does end to end with a payload from the same route.
    This test's server binds loopback only on an ephemeral port; D4 exchanges for real.
- Learned: (1) The `unchanged:`/rollback discipline B5 introduced for TCC grants transfers exactly
  to TLS material, and for the same reason: the thing being protected is a human-visible binding
  (there, the grant; here, the pin every paired client stores) that a silent rewrite destroys.
  (2) Asking the server whether it would admit an address - through its public API, in the test -
  is a better rule than copying its network list into the tool: the tool's own check can be simple
  and narrow as long as a node proves it never becomes wider. (3) A credential tool's most useful
  check is not on its own output but on the *disagreement between two places the value lives*: the
  file on disk and the process that loaded it.
- Blocker: none. TCC clicks (E3) remain the one irreducible human step.

  passes the certificate to `uvicorn.run`, so `--live` applies TLS to the *whole* listener

  to be a second unit on its own port, and the property worth protecting is that adding it leaves
  the first one byte-for-byte alone. One adapter serves both units and only the environment
  differs, so the two invocations cannot drift. `MOSS_WEB_PORT`/`MOSS_RUNS_DIR` are required flags
  under live mode with checked relations (not the batch port, not the batch runs dir), which is the

  - `leak-scan.sh` -> `leak-scan: clean`; `git diff --check` -> clean
  - `bash -n` on every `ops/*.sh` and `macos/scripts/*.sh` -> clean; the new script runs under

- Evidence:
  - **The batch invocation is recorded, not asserted loosely.** `BATCH_ARGV` in the new test file

  - `install-services.sh` derives its source from its own location, so it installs the checkout it

    without moving an inode, and the re-run also reports the *activation* as unchanged, because the
    test's `systemctl` stub remembers `enable`/`start` and answers `is-enabled`/`is-active` from
    that state.
  - The tool never restarts a running service. A changed unit file surfaces as
    `evidence: restart_required=<units>` instead, because bouncing the batch service is a
    deployment decision; that is recorded here so D3 does not mistake the absence of a restart for
    the absence of a change.
  - Ordering is checked positionally, not by prose: the replaced-unit node asserts the last
    `rollback:` line appears before the first `change:` line in stdout, then *executes* the printed
    rollback and gets the previous bytes back.
  - The PowerShell script cannot run on this host, so it is checked structurally by brace-matching

## Iteration 15 (run 20260728-023004-98501, its iteration 7) - app-owned latency probe (C3c)
- Target: Phase C candidate C3c - the last item before the C4 gate. The app (never the CLI) uses
  view authority, maps `committed_samples` to converted client capture timestamps, and emits only
  redacted p50/p95/max plus snapshot/events fetch timings, so the PRD's user-visible p95 gate stops
  being unfalsifiable.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/CaptureLatencyProbe.swift` (new),
  `CaptureController.swift` (one optional observer hook), `CaptureSecurity.swift` (`latency`
  command, `ControlChannelResponse.latency`, `latencyProbeUnavailable`), `CaptureCommandLine.swift`
  (allowlist + usage), `CaptureHTTPTransport.swift` (`liveURL` made internal so the probe reuses the
  route shape instead of copying it), `MOSSCaptureApp/main.swift` (the only composition root that
  builds the probe), `Tests/MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift`,
  `Tests/MTDCaptureCLITests/MTDCaptureCLITests.swift`, `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`.
  **No server source changed.**
- Method: the shape came from two facts read before writing anything. (1) The plan's Phase F
  procedure is a subtraction between a capture instant and a later instant, so both readings must
  come from one clock - which only exists inside the app, where the converted `capture_timestamp_ns`
  and the view token are co-located. (2) `live_mixer.py:139-169` defines the origin as the maximum
  first capture instant over lanes that have registered and are not failed, and freezes it into
  `_cursor_ns` at the first mix. So the probe derives the origin by the same rule rather than
  assuming the earliest frame or the start of capture. Splitting the file into a pure sampler (no
  clock, no network) and an IO probe is what makes the arithmetic testable to the nanosecond.
- Validation:
  - `swift test --filter 'Latency|AcknowledgedFrameObserver'` -> **10 passed** (9 core + 1 CLI)
  - `swift test --package-path macos/MOSSCapture` -> **131 passed, 0 failures** (was 121; +10)
  - `swift build --scratch-path <empty> --product MOSSCaptureApp --product mtd-capture` ->
    both products from an empty scratch path in **8.0 s with zero warnings**
  - `pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **536 passed, 2 skipped, 368 subtests** in 53.0s
    (unchanged - this iteration touched no Python)
  - `spikes/idea-044-attempt2-red-control/repro.py --target "$PWD"` -> **10/10**, unchanged
  - `leak-scan.sh` -> `leak-scan: clean`; `git diff --check` -> clean
- Evidence:
  - **The origin is derived, not assumed.** A node feeds mic-first-at-1.0 s and system-first-at-1.5 s
    and proves the mapping uses 1.5 s; another proves that with only one lane's frame in hand the
    report says `mixerOriginResolved: false` and produces *no* figures at all, then resolves when the
    second lane arrives and does not move when a lane later leaves. 16000 divides 1e9 exactly
    (asserted), so `origin + committed x 62500` is exact integer arithmetic and the mapping
    contributes no rounding to a gate measured in milliseconds.
  - **The first reading is a baseline, not a measurement.** Four advances after it yield exactly the
    four injected latencies; nearest-rank p50/p95/max are asserted as literals (300/400/500/900 ->
    p50 400, p95 900), so a percentile change is a test failure rather than a quieter number.
  - **The plan's four disqualifiers are counted, not averaged.** One node drives a negative reading,
    a backwards clock, and a post-discontinuity reading through the same sampler and asserts one
    surviving measurement plus `rejectedNegative=1`, `rejectedClockRegression=1`,
    `rejectedAfterTimelineBreak=1`, `timelineIntact=false`.
  - Found while writing the short-frame rule: "reject non-8000 frames" would have tainted every
    clean stop, because `CaptureController.stop` deliberately drains the trailing partial (B3). The
    general rule that actually distinguishes the two cases is *succession*: a short frame the lane
    continues past is a hole; a short frame with no successor ended the stream. A node asserts both
    directions.
  - **Secrecy is structural, not reviewed.** The report type has one string field (the schema name);
    everything else is a count, a flag or a duration - so there is no field a token could occupy. A
    node filters *all* headers of every issued request for the token and asserts the carrying set is
    exactly `["Authorization"]`, and asserts the encoded control response contains neither the token,
    the server host, nor the session id. The events body is decoded into `{seq}` only, so the
    transcript never enters the app's memory.
  - **Default-off is proven three ways**: constructing the probe schedules nothing and sends nothing;
    `measure()` with no running session schedules nothing and answers `polling: false`; a dispatcher
    built without a probe answers the typed `latencyProbeUnavailable` (this is what the CLI-side
    composition would get). Asking twice still schedules one poll.
  - **The measurement anchors to accepted audio.** The observer hook fires after
    `outbox.acknowledge`, and a node with an always-failing transport proves a retained frame is
    never observed while the same frame through a working transport is observed exactly once with
    its wire facts intact. The hook takes lane/timestamp/rate/count/discontinuity rather than a
    `CaptureFrame`, so nothing on this path can reach the PCM; a source gate asserts the probe file
    contains no `pcm16`/`pcm_base64`/`loadCaptureBearerToken`.
  - Mutation rehearsal 1 (`origins.max()` -> `.min()`): 4 assertions fail. Reverted.
  - Mutation rehearsal 2 (copy the view token into a second request header): 2 assertions fail -
    *after* the node was strengthened. The first attempt at this rehearsal passed, because the node
    only checked the URL; the all-headers check exists because the mutation found the gap.
  - Mutation rehearsal 3 (observe the frame before the publish/ack): 3 assertions fail. Reverted.
  - Mutation rehearsal 4 (drop the `current.running` guard so `measure()` always polls): 3 fail.
  - Mutation rehearsal 5 (count readings after a timeline break): 1 fails. Reverted.
  - Mutation rehearsal 6 (drop the 1 s portal cycle from the render bound): 2 fail. Reverted.
  - Mutation rehearsal 7 (wait for a failed lane the mixer already excluded): 6 fail. Reverted.
- Learned: (1) Reading the *server's* origin rule before writing the client's was the whole
  iteration - "first frame seen" and "start of capture" are both wrong, and either would have
  produced a plausible latency figure that was silently offset by the lanes' start skew.
  (2) A mutation rehearsal is worth running even when the node looks obviously sufficient: the
  token-secrecy node passed a real leak (a second header) until the assertion was changed from "not
  in the URL" to "in exactly one header".
  (3) Handing an observer facts instead of the frame is cheaper than auditing what the observer does
  with the frame - the PCM is simply not reachable from that call.
- Blocker: none. TCC clicks (E3) remain the one irreducible human step.
- Next: C4 - the final local gate and the single keeper merge. Run the Swift, full Python, tracer and

  (5 s outage / ambiguous retry / duplicate retry / 429 / outbox overflow), then
  `RALPH_MERGE_DRY_RUN=1 bash scripts/ralph-afk/merge-keeper.sh` followed by the real run, and record
  both the feature tip and merge SHAs.

  reading either unit file. (2) A descriptor fetched from the running service is the only proof the

    order and the MOSS keychain is appended fourth; `moss_entries=1` after the idempotent re-run, so

    self-signed `CN=MOSS Capture Local Signing`, RSA 2048 / sha256WithRSAEncryption,
    `X509v3 Basic Constraints: critical CA:FALSE`, `Key Usage: critical Digital Signature`,
    `Extended Key Usage: critical Code Signing`, notBefore 2026-07-28 05:05:08 GMT →
    notAfter 2036-07-25 05:05:08 GMT.
  - **The PRD's "DR unchanged across a rebuild" property, measured at the identity level.** Two
    *different* binaries (`/usr/bin/true`, `/bin/echo`) signed with the same `--identifier` both
    emit `designated => identifier "com.alphasight.moss.capture" and certificate leaf =
    H"e118d874377746c4bd25beb8252bb84302b73e72"`, byte-identical, while their `CDHash` values differ
    (`acf92317…` vs `4f4391fc…`) — so the DR is demonstrably not cdhash-derived. Re-signing changed
    bytes at the *same path* (a stand-in for a rebuild) leaves the DR byte-identical. The `H"…"`
    value equals `shasum -a 1` of the certificate's DER, computed independently from
    `security find-certificate | openssl x509 -outform DER` → `e118d874377746c4bd25beb8252bb84302b73e72`.
    Ad-hoc contrast measured in the same session: `codesign --sign -` on the same two binaries gives
    `designated => cdhash H"…" or cdhash H"…"` with different hashes per binary — which is exactly
    the TCC-grant-invalidating behavior the tool's header says a certificate identity avoids.
  - **Never gate on `find-identity`, reproduced on m4mbp**: `security find-identity -v -p codesigning`
    reports `1 valid identities found` and lists only the pre-existing `LiveTranscribe Local Dev` —
    the MOSS identity is absent from that list while `codesign` signs with it successfully. The
    iteration-9 MacStudio finding holds on this host too.
  - **No trust change**: the MOSS certificate is in neither the user nor the admin trust-settings
    domain (`security dump-trust-settings` / `-d` → `moss_in_*_trust_settings=0`). The three certs
    that do carry user trust settings (`LiveTranscribe Local Dev`, `Ga0-Alienware-RTX4070Ti`,
    `Ga0-RTX4090`) are pre-existing and unrelated. No SIP, Gatekeeper or global trust change.
  - **Idempotence**: a second run printed `unchanged: codesign already signs with 'MOSS Capture Local
    Signing' …` plus the same eight `evidence:` lines, no `change:` line, and left the password
    file's inode/size/mtime and the keychain's inode untouched.
  - **Rollback rehearsed for real, then re-applied.** `security delete-keychain … && rm -f <password>`
    removed both files and restored the search list to exactly the three pre-existing entries
    (`moss_entries=0`, default keychain untouched); re-running the tool from that clean state
    rebuilt everything with `change:` ×4 and exit 0.
  - **Secret hygiene**: the keychain password appears in no shell history (`.zsh_history`,
    `.bash_history` → 0), in no file under `~/Library/Logs`, and in no process argv
    (`ps_hits_excluding_self=0`; the first measurement's `ps_hits=1` was my own `grep -F "$P"`
    matching its own command line, not a leak). Its only occurrence on disk is the 0600 file inside
    a 0700 directory. No token, payload or pin is involved in E1.
  - **Checkout undisturbed**: m4mbp still `f9285d69ed7bcc592bb41b3dcdf29e3221968f44`, `dirty=0`.
- Learned:
  1. **The signing identity is not reproducible, and that changes when the rollback is free.** The
     rehearsal minted a new RSA key, so the leaf moved `8c99754e…` → `ef8fa542…` and the DR with it.
     The lab bundle's identity is a function of its inputs; this one is a function of a stored
     private key. So E1's rollback is free **only until E2b signs the installed bundle** — after E3
     it would destroy the human's TCC grants. Recorded on the E1/E2b candidates, not just here.
  2. **A fresh SSH session finds the keychain locked**, even though `set-keychain-settings` disabled
     the auto-lock timeout: `security show-keychain-info` answers `User interaction is not allowed`
     and `codesign --sign` fails `errSecInternalComponent`. The unlock state is per security session,
     not a keychain setting. My first DR probe failed this way and looked like a broken identity;
     the tool's own probe and `build-app.sh:186-191` both unlock first, so nothing in the pipeline is
     affected — but any hand-run `codesign` from a new session must unlock, and that is now in the
     Validation section.
  3. **A guard that shadows another guard is not exercised by the obvious input.** `System.keychain`
     tests the basename branch, not the system-directory branch, because the basename check runs
     first; only a non-system *name* in `/Library/Keychains` reaches the directory branch. Worth
     remembering for the other tools' refusal rehearsals.
  4. **Exit codes measured through a pipe are the pipe's.** The first refusal rehearsal reported
     `rc=0` because `$?` followed `tail`, not the script; re-measured without a pipe both refusals
     are exit 1. Never record a refusal's exit code from a pipeline.
- Blocker: none new. E3's TCC clicks remain the one irreducible human step.
- Next: E2b — run the reviewed `macos/scripts/build-app.sh` then `install-app.sh` on m4mbp to build,
  sign and install `/Applications/MOSSCapture.app` plus `mtd-capture`. Record the rollback before
  mutating (`install-app.sh` moves a replaced bundle to `<installed>.backup-<utc>`; on a first
  install the rollback is `rm -rf /Applications/MOSSCapture.app` plus the CLI path). Expect the
  bundle DR to be `identifier "com.alphasight.moss.capture" and certificate leaf = H"e118d874…"`,
  identifier `com.alphasight.moss.capture`, and `keychain-access-groups` **absent** from the embedded
  entitlements. Check whether `~/.local/bin` is on m4mbp's PATH first and pass `--bin-dir` if not,
  rather than editing a shell profile. Build both Swift products with **separate** `--product`
  invocations. State C4 review note (a) when `build-app.sh` unlocks the keychain with the password
  on argv. After this step the E1 rollback stops being free.

### Findings that changed the runbook (all derived from the reviewed source at f9285d6)
1. **The TCC grants do NOT have to happen inside D4's five-minute pairing window.**
   `CaptureController.start` (`CaptureController.swift:230-246`) requires only
   `loadControlSecret() != nil` - which the app writes for itself at launch - and calls
   `source.start` at `:242`, *before* the first publish at `:250`. Pairing is needed only by that
   publish. So an **unpaired** `start` still raises both prompts; the publish then fails
   `missingCaptureBearer`, which `CaptureFrameRetryPolicy` classes as not retryable, so the
   controller unwinds the source and throws - but the user's two decisions are already durable,
   because TCC records the click, not the capture outcome. Both iteration 22's "Next" note and the
   old E3 candidate asserted the opposite coupling. Splitting them removes the worst failure mode of
   the human step: a mis-timed prompt answer can no longer burn a minted payload.
   **Derived, not observed** - E3 itself is the confirmation; if the unpaired `start` behaves
   differently, fall back to the coupled sequence (mint, pair, then start once).
2. **Prompt order is fixed by the source, not by chance.** `NativeDualCaptureSource.start` admits
   system audio first (`:191`), microphone second (`:192`). System audio has no request API -
   `AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap` inside `SystemAudioTap.start` *is* the request, called inline on
   the control thread - while the microphone is the asynchronous
   `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .audio)` that leaves the lane `pending`. So System Audio
   Recording is always the first alert, and it is the only one that can block.
3. **The CLI cannot launch the app on this host, and nothing says so anywhere.**
   `NSWorkspaceLaunchServicesCaptureAppLauncher.launch()` (`CaptureCommandLine.swift:69`) reads
   `MOSS_CAPTURE_APP_URL` and throws `launchServicesUnavailable` when it is unset. Nothing in the
   product, in `install-app.sh` or in a shell profile sets it - the only occurrences in the tree are
   two test fixtures and one `env.pop` in `tests/live_integration_replay.py`. That is exactly why
   the installed CLI answered `{"ok":false}` `rc=70` in iteration 22: not "no helper running" as
   recorded, but "no helper running **and** no way to start one". Had the operator been handed
   `mtd-capture pair` as the first command, it would have failed with an opaque `{"ok":false}` and
   burned the 300 s payload. The runbook therefore starts with an explicit GUI launch.
4. **A hung `start` is the expected appearance of an unanswered prompt.**
   `UnixDomainControlServer.serve()` is a serial accept loop (`CaptureSecurity.swift:897-902`) and
   `UnixDomainControlClient` sets no `SO_RCVTIMEO` (no timeout symbol exists in that file). So while
   the tap call waits on the alert, `start` blocks with no timeout and every other `mtd-capture`
   command - `status` included - queues behind it. This is M36's consequence made concrete: a hung
   `status` is not evidence the app died. Diagnose with `pgrep`/`sample`, never by killing the app.
5. **The pairing payload is a stdin argument.** `CaptureCommandLine.swift:114-130`: `pair` takes
   `--server` from argv and the payload from `input.readAll()`, with empty stdin -> `rc=65`. Pasting
   it into an interactive `mtd-capture pair` and pressing Ctrl-D satisfies the PRD's secret-hygiene
   clause for free - no argv, no file, no history entry.

### The verification finding: TCC state is readable read-only, and the grant carries the DR
- `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db` on m4mbp is `-rw-r--r-- ga0:staff`, 163840
  bytes, and opens over plain SSH **without** Full Disk Access. Proven non-vacuously before any
  conclusion was drawn from it: `select count(*) from access` -> **320**, and the service histogram
  lists 20 services. (A zero-row answer and a failed open look identical; iteration 22's learning 4
  is exactly this class of error, so the reader was proven first.)
- The service names are read off that live table, not guessed: Microphone is
  `kTCCServiceMicrophone` (21 rows) and **System Audio Recording is `kTCCServiceAudioCapture`**
  (3 rows). `auth_value` 2 = allowed, 0 = denied, both present on this host
  (`com.openai.chat|2` vs `com.google.antigravity|0`, `com.microsoft.rdc.macos|0`). `client_type`
  0 = bundle identifier, 1 = absolute path.
- **The csreq column stores the designated requirement.** Each row carries a `FADE0C00` code
  requirement blob; `sqlite3 … writefile()` + `csreq -r <file> -t` decodes it. Decoded on the
  `com.livetranscribe.app` precedent - a locally-signed app already holding **both** grants on this
  same machine - it reads
  `identifier "com.livetranscribe.app" and certificate leaf = H"51e289ba70a36bcdd063f1efa660d56aebd83da7"`,
  80 bytes. That is byte-for-byte the *form* of the E1 DR. So after E3 the moss rows must decode to
  `identifier "com.alphasight.moss.capture" and certificate leaf = H"e118d874377746c4bd25beb8252bb84302b73e72"`,
  and that decode is the **direct observation** - in TCC's own storage - that the grants key on the
  DR rather than the cdhash. Until now iterations 21/22 could only argue that link from the DR's
  stability across three byte-different builds; this makes it checkable.
  It also means the precedent app proves the *whole scheme* works on this host: a self-signed
  local identity can hold System Audio Recording here.
- Consequence for the loop: the PRD's "Permissions granted" clause becomes a two-command read-only
  check the loop can run itself the moment the operator reports back, with no TCC write, no
  `tccutil`, and no reliance on the operator's description of what they clicked.
- Validation of this iteration's own claims: the decode command was run for real (output above), the
  reader was proven with a row count, the temp directory was removed and its absence asserted, and
  the three service probes returned 200/200/200. `git status --porcelain` on m4mbp still 0 lines.
- Learned:
  1. **"Record the blocker" is not the same as "stop".** The PRD says record the click sequence and
     move on. The useful work was not writing the sentence "a human must click Allow" - it was
     reading the source hard enough to find that the click sequence is System-Audio-then-Microphone,
     that the CLI cannot launch the app, and that the clicks are not actually bound to the 300 s
     window. A blocker is worth as much as the runbook attached to it.
  2. **A read-only path to the evidence often exists where a write path is forbidden.** The PRD bans
     touching the TCC database; it does not ban reading it, and the user-domain file turned out to be
     world-readable. That converts the one acceptance clause the loop cannot cause into one it can
     still verify. Worth asking of every "unscriptable" gate.
  3. **An empty query result is not evidence until the query is proven to work.** Same shape as
     iteration 22's vacuous CDHash comparison and iteration 21's exit-code-through-a-pipe slip: the
     `%moss%` baseline of zero rows means "undetermined" only because `count(*)` returned 320 first.
  4. **A tool's error string can hide a missing precondition.** `{"ok":false}` `rc=70` was recorded
     in iteration 22 as "no helper running", which is true but incomplete - the CLI also had no way
     to start one, because `MOSS_CAPTURE_APP_URL` is unset everywhere. The generic error made the
     two cases indistinguishable from the outside.
- Blocker: **E3's two GUI clicks on m4mbp** - the exact sequence is above. Nothing else in the loop
  is blocked on input the loop cannot obtain; F1-F4 are blocked only on E3's outcome, which is a
  human action rather than missing information.
- Next: after the operator confirms both grants, run the two read-only TCC verifications to close the
  PRD's "Permissions granted" clause, then D4 (mint on the host, pair on m4mbp inside 300 s, confirm
  `live/live-auth.json` appears 0600 on ext4 and no payload reached history/logs/argv/journal), then
  F1's 60 s canary. If the operator is unavailable for a long stretch, the one candidate that needs
  no human and no TCC is F4's rollback rehearsal - but it takes the live service down and must not be
  started while a pairing or canary window is open, so prefer waiting.

[loop 20260728-023004-98501] blocked at iteration 15

## Supervisor diagnosis - ATS blocks the signed app bundle (2026-07-28, operator-attended)
- Context: not a loop iteration. The operator ran the E3 runbook, pairing failed, and this entry
  records the diagnosis performed with them. No tracked product source was changed.
- Trigger: the runbook's step order was wrong. `captureConfiguration(from:)`
  (`CaptureSecurity.swift:847-862`) throws `missingCaptureConfiguration` before
  `CaptureController.start` runs, so an unpaired `start` can never raise the TCC prompts. Iteration
  23's finding 1 predicted the opposite and flagged itself "Derived, not observed" - the fallback it
  named (pair first, then start) is correct and is now the order in Phase G's runbook.
- Defect A, fixed procedurally, still a product bug (candidate G2): pasting the payload and pressing
  Return before Ctrl-D yields `invalidPinnedHash`. `CapturePairingPayload.init` never trims, so the
  pin field is 65 bytes against a strict `count == 64` check. Measured: 64 without the newline, 65
  with. No test covers whitespace. Operator workaround: `IFS= read -r payload` then
  `printf '%s' "$payload" | mtd-capture pair --server ...` - payload stays off argv, out of `ps`
  and out of shell history.
- Defect B (candidate G1), the real blocker. After the trim, pairing failed `control_failed`, and
  the server never logged `POST /api/live/pairings` at all. Isolated by A/B on m4mbp, each step
  measured rather than argued:
  - bare binary, pinned GET to `https://100.64.0.8:7861/api/live/descriptor` -> **200**
  - real `URLSessionCapturePairingExchangeAdapter` (throwaway package depending on the repo by
    path, so the repo was untouched) -> **paired**, session + bearer + view token returned
  - unsigned `.build/debug/MOSSCaptureApp` + `mtd-capture pair` -> **{"ok":true}**
  - installed `/Applications/MOSSCapture.app` -> **control_failed**
  - minimal ad-hoc `.app` bundle wrapping the same probe binary -> **-1200 / -9802**, after the
    delegate had printed `pin MATCH -> accepting`
  - that same bundle + `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` -> **200**
  Root cause: ATS applies to `.app` bundles and not to bare binaries, and overrides the pinning
  delegate's acceptance because the leaf is not CA-chained. Ruled out first, each by direct test:
  wrong pin (m4mbp, served leaf and payload all `a35ca9fc...b680ff`), network path (`/live` and
  descriptor both 200 from m4mbp), TCC/Local Network (fails identically under the terminal's
  identity; not listed in Local Network settings), hardened runtime (ad-hoc + runtime -> 200),
  entitlements (ad-hoc + runtime + `audio-input` -> 200), sandboxing (no `app-sandbox` embedded),
  application firewall (disabled) and network filters (only a Logitech HID extension).
- Defect C (candidate G3): `sanitizedControlError` reduces every unrecognised error to
  `control_failed` and `MOSSCaptureApp/main.swift` logs nothing at all. The `-1200`/`-9802` was
  available from the first failed attempt and was discarded at the boundary. This is why B took
  hours instead of minutes.
- Why no gate caught B: `_private_non_loopback_ipv4()` (`tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py:690`)
  returns MacStudio's 192.168.x address, which ATS exempts as local networking. Production dials
  100.64.0.8 (Tailscale CGNAT), which ATS does not exempt. The tracer lists `100.64.0.0/10` among

## Iteration 1 (run 20260728-072601-15601) - G1: the ATS declaration, and the measurement that
## showed the planned regression test could never have caught it
- Target: candidate G1 from the prd.md amendment of 2026-07-28 - the App Transport Security
  declaration that lets the app's pinned live transport work from an `.app` bundle - together with
  G4's "tracer case bound to a 100.64.0.0/10 address", because a fix wants its gate in the same
  change.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Resources/Info.plist` (+16),
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/MTDCaptureCLITests/MTDCaptureCLITests.swift` (+30),
  `tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py` (+219/-6), `tests/test_macos_packaging_tools.py` (+7),
  `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`. First tracked product change since the keeper
  merge, authorized by the amendment and inside its four items.

### What was measured, before anything was fixed
The planned regression test was written first and it **passed red** - it could not see the bug. So
the next step was to find out why, with one disposable ad-hoc `.app`-bundled Swift probe in /tmp
whose URLSessionDelegate accepts any leaf (built, measured, deleted; nothing entered the repo).
Matrix on MacStudio (macOS 26.5.1; m4mbp is 26.5.2 and answered identically on the one row it
shares):
  | destination                        | bare binary | inside an `.app` |
  | remote 100.64.0.8   (tailnet)      | 200         | **-1200 / -9802** |
  | remote 192.168.68.38 (LAN)         | 200         | 200               |
  | this host's own 100.64.0.1         | 200         | 200               |
  | this host's own 192.168.68.36      | 200         | 200               |
Then the fix, on the same bundle, changing nothing else: `NSAppTransportSecurity =
{NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: true}` -> remote 100.64.0.8 answers **200**. That is the red/green pair
for G1, measured directly rather than argued.
Two things follow, and the second one contradicts the plan:
1. ATS applies to a bundle and not to a bare executable, and it overrides a delegate that has
   already accepted the leaf. Confirmed independently of m4mbp.
2. **The exemption is loopback + RFC 1918, not "the address range the tracer picks".** A server the
   tracer starts is on the tracer's host, so however its peer address is written the connection is
   routed over loopback and exempted - `100.64.0.1` (this host's own tailnet address) proves that
   directly. G4's premise, that binding `100.64.0.0/10` would reproduce the failure, is wrong. And
   the supervisor's diagnosis was only half right: remote RFC 1918 is exempt too, so even a second
   LAN host would not have caught this. **No single-host test can gate ATS.**

### What was built instead
- The fix: `Resources/Info.plist` declares `NSAppTransportSecurity = {NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: true}`
  and nothing else, with a comment carrying the failure signature and the reason a scoped
  `NSExceptionDomains` entry was rejected (it would bake one deployment's hostname into the shipped
  product; the exact-leaf pin is the security control by prd.md design).
  The sibling trap is called out in every gate: declaring `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` or either
  `NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsIn*` key makes the OS ignore `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads`.
- Three shape gates, since a behavioral one is impossible here:
  1. `MTDCaptureCLITests.testBundleDeclaresTheTransportExceptionThePinnedClientCannotWorkWithout` -
     **parses** the plist rather than substring-matching it, so the explanatory comment inside the
     plist cannot satisfy the assertion, and requires the key set to be exactly
     `["NSAllowsArbitraryLoads"]`.
  2. `test_macos_packaging_tools.py` - asserts it on the bundle `build-app.sh` *composes*, which is
     the artifact E2b installs, not on the tracked source.
  3. `_first_install_lab_bundle` - refuses to install a lab bundle whose product plist lacks it.
- The CGNAT tracer node was kept but renamed to what it can honestly prove:
  `test_bundled_app_on_the_production_address_range_still_refuses_an_unpinned_leaf`. Its docstring
  states that it does **not** observe ATS and why. What it does prove is the other half of the
  declaration's safety case: with ATS off the entire trust decision belongs to
  `PinnedCertificateURLSessionDelegate`, so the node pairs once honestly over the production
  address range and then serves a certificate the pairing payload's pin does not describe and
  requires refusal.
- One adjacent defect found and closed on the way: the lab bundle's reuse predicate keyed only on
  the built executable's Mach-O identity, so a product-Info.plist edit changed the installed bundle
  without triggering a reinstall - the tracer would have failed its own continuity assertions
  instead, and a passing run could have been driving a bundle the product no longer describes. The
  predicate now also keys on `product_info_plist_sha256`, recorded in the evidence file.

  2. `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` added beside it -> the **2 exact-shape nodes fail**; the tracer's

### Learned
1. **A regression test that passes on the first run is a measurement, not a success.** Writing the
   planned test first is what surfaced that the plan's premise was wrong; had it been written after
   the fix it would have been recorded as proof and shipped a gate that gates nothing.
2. **Ask what the environment exempts, not only what the code does.** Two independent exemptions
   were in play (bundle-vs-bare and loopback/RFC1918-vs-everything else) and the second one is
   invisible to any test that starts its own server. The blind spot was not the tracer's address
   picker; it was that the tracer is its own peer.
3. **When a behavioral gate is impossible, say so in the test.** The honest move was to rename the
   node to what it proves and write the impossibility into its docstring and into context.md, so
   the next reader does not re-derive it or, worse, trust it.

## Iteration 2 (run 20260728-072601-15601) - G2: the pairing payload is trimmed, and the trimmed
## payload is the one that goes on the wire
- Target: candidate G2 from the prd.md amendment of 2026-07-28 - the pairing-payload whitespace
  defect that turned an operator's Return into `invalidPinnedHash`, an error blaming the server's
  certificate for a keystroke.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/CaptureSecurity.swift` (+31/-3),
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift` (+85),
  `tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py` (+6/-1), `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`.

### The second half of the defect, found while fixing the first
Trimming in `CapturePairingPayload.init` alone would have been a half-fix.
`URLSessionCapturePairingExchangeAdapter.pair` parsed the payload for the pin and then put the
**raw stdin bytes** in the HTTP body (`String(decoding: pairingPayload, as: UTF8.self)`) - the
client validated one string and transmitted another. Read against the server: `live_auth.
_normalize_cert_sha256` does `.strip().lower()` on the pin field but nothing strips the prefix, so
a trailing newline would have been forgiven on the wire while a leading space would have come back
as 401, which the app surfaces only as `nonSuccessStatus(401)` - a second whitespace fault wearing
a second wrong error. The adapter now sends `parsedPayload.wireRepresentation`.
Three changes, all in one parse:
1. trim `.whitespacesAndNewlines` before splitting; whitespace-only input is `missingPairingPayload`;
2. whitespace that survives the trim is *inside* a field, so refuse it as `invalidPairingPayload`
   rather than letting it reach the strict 64-hex check and blame the certificate again;
3. `wireRepresentation` = `"mtd1.<secret>.<lowercased pin>"` is what is transmitted.
Safety of the trim was checked against the generator, not assumed: the secret is
`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, no dot, no whitespace) and both sides lowercase the
pin, so canonicalization cannot eat a legitimate character.

### Validation
- `swift test --package-path macos/MOSSCapture` -> **134 passed / 0 failures** (was 132).
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py -q` -> **4 passed**, 0 skips, 14.3 s.
- `python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **537 passed / 2 skipped / 368 subtests** in
  60.9 s (unchanged count: the tracer node was strengthened in place, not added to).
- Both Swift products build, separate invocations, zero warnings.
- Phase A attempt-2 discriminator **10/10**; `leak-scan: clean`.
- Mutation rehearsals, each applied and reverted:
  1. wire form reverted to the raw bytes -> the body assertion fails on all four typed forms,
     showing `mtd1.secret.aaaa…\n` (and `\r\n`, and the indented form) actually on the wire.
  2. trim removed -> the trailing-newline node fails; through the **real process path** the tracer's
     `mtd-capture pair` answers `exit=70 {"ok":false,"error":"invalidPairingPayload"}`.
  3. trim *and* the internal-whitespace guard removed -> the same input reproduces the shipped
     signature exactly: `invalidPinnedHash`. The same mutation also crashed the whitespace node's
     stub client on `removeFirst` from an empty response queue - i.e. without the guard a payload
     with a space inside the secret really does reach the network.
- Nothing outside the repo was mutated: no host touched, no service restarted, no payload minted,
  no app rebuilt or reinstalled on m4mbp.

### Learned
1. **A canonicalization that does not reach the wire is not a fix.** The parse and the transmission
   have to be the same string; anywhere they diverge, the validation applies to a string the peer
   never sees. Grepping for the *other* use of the raw input was what turned a one-line trim into
   the actual fix.
2. **Check the tolerant peer before deciding what the fix must cover.** The server strips the pin
   and not the prefix, so trailing and leading whitespace fail in two different places with two
   different error shapes. Only reading `_normalize_cert_sha256` made that asymmetry visible.
3. **Put the operator's keystrokes into the existing real-process node instead of adding one.**
   Feeding the tracer's second pairing `payload + b"\n"` covers stdin -> UDS -> app -> HTTPS at zero
   extra runtime, and it is the node that proved mutation 2 for real rather than in a stub.
- Blocker: unchanged and still the only one - E3's two GUI clicks on m4mbp. G2 does not need them.
- Next: **G3** - classify `URLError`/`NSError` into a typed non-secret shape (domain + code, never a
  token or payload) and log unclassified control-channel failures in `MOSSCaptureApp/main.swift`,
  which is what would have shown `-1200/-9802` on the first attempt; then G4's full client gate and
  the single authorized merge through `merge-keeper.sh`. After the merge, re-run E2b on m4mbp so the
  installed app carries G1+G2+G3, then the corrected E3 order (pair first, then start, then clicks).

## Iteration 3 (run 20260728-072601-15601) - G3: a failure the control channel cannot name now
## says which failure it is, and the app records it
- Target: candidate G3 from the prd.md amendment of 2026-07-28 - `sanitizedControlError` mapped
  every unrecognised error to the bare string `control_failed` and `MOSSCaptureApp/main.swift`
  logged nothing at all, so the ATS block reached the operator as four words and survived a merge.
- Files: `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/CaptureSecurity.swift` (+148/-9),
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureCore/CaptureCommandLine.swift` (+1/-1),
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Sources/MOSSCaptureApp/main.swift` (+3),
  `macos/MOSSCapture/Tests/MOSSCaptureCoreTests/CaptureControllerTests.swift` (+307),
  `tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py` (+19), `scripts/ralph-afk/{context.md,progress.txt}`.

### What was built
`classifyControlError` replaces `sanitizedControlError` and returns `(name, detail)`. The four
typed families keep their exact `String(describing:)` names and get **no** detail - their cases
carry only what this process put in them, so the name already is the evidence, and a detail beside
one would be noise. Everything else keeps the bare `control_failed` it always had **plus** a
`ControlChannelErrorDetail{domain, code, underlyingCode?}` built from `error as NSError`. Building
it from the bridge rather than from a type list is the point: `URLError`, `POSIXError` and a bare
Swift struct all answer, so this is a backstop instead of another list the next unfamiliar error
falls off the end of. `underlyingCode` is `_kCFStreamErrorCodeKey` when non-zero, else
`NSUnderlyingError.code`, else absent - never zeroed, because zero is a code an error can have.
`UnixDomainControlServer` gained an optional `ControlChannelFailureLogging` and calls it **only**
for a detail-bearing failure; the app wires `OSLogControlChannelFailureLog()`, the CLI has no
control server. Unified logging is the only surface an `LSUIElement` app has - no window, and
Launch Services gives it no usable stderr:
  log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.alphasight.moss.capture"' --last 30m
Everything that line marks `.public` is provably non-secret. The detail is numbers and a constant;
the command word is reduced to `ControlChannelCommands.all` or the literal `other`. That constant
also replaced the CLI's duplicate command literal, so the log's public vocabulary and the CLI's
accepted set are now one list rather than two that can drift.

### The distinction this buys, measured through the real process
The tracer's pin refusal answers `control_failed` + `{domain: NSURLErrorDomain, code: -999}` with
no `underlyingCode`. -999 is `NSURLErrorCancelled`: the pinning delegate cancelled the challenge,
so *this client* refused the leaf. The ATS block G1 fixed is -1200 with underlying -9802: the *OS*
refused the connection. Both were `control_failed` before this iteration, and telling them apart
is exactly the diagnosis nobody could make in E3. The tracer node was strengthened in place to
assert that signature rather than only `returncode != 0`.

### Validation
- `swift test --package-path macos/MOSSCapture` -> **139 passed / 0 failures** (was 134).
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_macos_uds_tracer.py -q` -> **4 passed**, 0 skips, 14.9 s.
- `python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> **537 passed / 2 skipped / 368 subtests** in
  63.1 s (unchanged count: the tracer node was strengthened in place, not added to).
- Both Swift products from an **empty** scratch path, separate invocations: mtd-capture 8.2 s,
  MOSSCaptureApp 0.7 s, **zero warnings**.
- Phase A attempt-2 discriminator **10/10**; `leak-scan: clean`.
- Mutation rehearsals, each applied and reverted:
  1. default branch returns a nil detail -> **2 nodes / 7 assertions** fail across all three
     NSError shapes and the log node.
  2. the `failureLog?.recordUnclassifiedFailure` call removed -> the log node fails with 0 records
     against 2; the response node still passes, so the two halves are gated independently.
  3. the log emits the raw command instead of the bounded one -> the fixed-vocabulary node fails
     showing `control command status; token=sk-live-do-not-log …` in the emitted line.
  4. `domain = nsError.description` instead of `nsError.domain` -> the absence assertions fire with
     `https://100.64.0.8:7861/api/live/pairings` and the whole SSL message on the wire. That is the
     leak this shape exists to prevent, reproduced rather than argued.
- Nothing outside the repo was mutated: no host touched, no service restarted, no payload minted,
  no app rebuilt or reinstalled on m4mbp. Nothing was written to the unified log by the suite - the
  log node drives the injected `emit`, not `Logger`.

### Learned
1. **The classifier's default branch is where the diagnosis dies, and it is reachable by
   construction.** Four typed families were listed; everything the OS raises fell through. Building
   the fallback from the `NSError` bridge instead of from a fifth `case` is what stops the same
   hole reopening for the next unfamiliar error type.
2. **Deciding what is safe to log is easier than sanitising what was logged.** The protocol is
   handed a command word and a `ControlChannelErrorDetail` and nothing else, so an implementation
   cannot write a payload even by accident. Mutation 4 shows the alternative: one field widened
   from `domain` to `description` and the deployment's URL is on the wire.
3. **Bound the public vocabulary even where the input cannot currently be hostile.** An unknown
   command throws a named error and never reaches the log, so the `other` guard is unreachable
   today - and it is the guard that keeps the claim "everything public here is non-secret" true if
   that ever changes.
- Blocker: unchanged and still the only one - E3's two GUI clicks on m4mbp. G3 does not need them.
- Next: **G4** - the amendment's last item. Re-run the full client gate (both products from an
  empty scratch path, `swift test`, `pytest tests`, tracer, discriminator, leak-scan, clean tree)

  and satisfy it honestly rather than raising `RALPH_MERGE_MAIN_BEFORE` to get past it. After the
  merge, re-run E2b on m4mbp so the installed app carries G1+G2+G3, then the corrected E3 order

### The gate, measured on MacStudio 2026-07-28 at product tree 23dc163 (tree clean before and after)
