Iteration 24 of run 20260728-181020 - PRE-RUN RECORD, written and committed BEFORE
the host is touched: the no-mutation contract for the decode-cap latency probe.
================================================================================

prd.md requires every server or Mac mutation to have its rollback recorded before it is
applied. This probe's answer is that it performs NO mutation, and the claim is stated
here in advance so it can be checked against rather than asserted afterwards.

WHAT THE PROBE DOES ON THE HOST:
  - sends inference requests to the ALREADY-RESIDENT vLLM at http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1,
    the same endpoint `live-identity-seam-probe.py` has used since H4 and the same one
    the live service itself decodes through;
  - reads `~/.local/share/moss-transcribe-diarize/live/golden.wav` read-only;
  - writes span WAVs only inside a TemporaryDirectory it creates and its own context
    manager removes, under a scratch dir OUTSIDE /tmp/mtd-live-* so the standing host
    check for stray live scratch keeps its meaning.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, each of which is the thing that would need a rollback:
  no pairing code, no device row, no live session, no view token, no auth-state write,
  no checkout, no merge, no push, no deploy, no systemctl, no unit file, no manifest
  write, no TLS material, no app install, no product source change, no restart.
  Therefore: ROLLBACK REQUIRED = NONE. There is no host state to put back.

THE ONE REAL COST, stated because it is not zero: GPU time on the shared engine. The
uncapped condition deliberately generates to the pre-D-c 2048-token bound, ~8.5 s per
request at F1's measured rate, and the run makes at most 9 requests (1 warm-up + 2 x 3
conditions), i.e. under ~1 minute of GPU. Batch and live share that engine, so the
baseline below must show no live session and no running batch job BEFORE the first
request, and the after-check must show both services' MainPIDs and NRestarts unmoved.

STOP CONDITIONS - abandon the run and record a blocker rather than pressing on:
  - any live session is active, or a batch job is running, at baseline;
  - moss-live-web / moss-web / moss-vllm MainPID or NRestarts differs from baseline;
  - `git rev-parse HEAD` on the host is not 77e0014;
  - a journal traceback appears that was not in the baseline.

VALIDITY FENCE, per the standing rule (compare against the DEPLOYED sha, never main):
  git diff --name-only 77e0014 HEAD -- ':!scripts/ralph-afk'   must be EMPTY, or the
  product function the probe imports is not the one the service runs.

THE INSTRUMENT: scripts/ralph-afk/decode-cap-latency-probe.py (new, tracked).
It does not wait for a runaway - it induces one, then runs a PAIRED comparison over the
same audio through the product's own RunnerBoundedWavInference.transcribe_pcm seam with a
real FrozenSpan of the contract's 40000 samples. Only _token_cap differs:
  A "pre-D-c"  - overridden to 2048, the bound actually in force before iteration 16.
                 A semantic revert of D-c, inside the probe.
  B "deployed" - the product's own canonical_decode_token_cap, IMPORTED not restated
                 (iteration 23's rule), which returns 286 for a 2.5 s span.
Plus a control with no trigger at all, because a cap that truncates real speech would be
worse than the runaway it prevents.

VALIDATED OFFLINE ON ELEVEN SYNTHETIC CASES (33 checks) BEFORE EACH HOST RUN, with a
stubbed engine. That validation earned its keep three times:
  - it caught VllmRunner's constructor being model=, not model_path=, before any host call;
  - case 7 encodes host failure 1 (a trigger that SUPPRESSES generation must reduce to
    INCONCLUSIVE, never to a 1.0x speedup between two empty decodes);
  - case 10 encodes host failure 2 (the engine runs away but the product reports 0 tokens;
    the runaway must still be detected, at the engine seam).

THE MEASUREMENT, on the deployed 77e0014, span sha256 844e6eff…, temperature=2.0 seed=
20260728, 3 repeats per condition, warm-up decode discarded first (iteration 23's lesson):

  condition              tokens      wall median          RTF
  control, no trigger      49        0.198 s              0.081
  A pre-D-c 2048         2048 (3/3)  8.129 s (8.036-8.192) 3.277
  B deployed cap 286      286 (3/3)  1.074 s (1.071-1.077) 0.431

  => 7.571x, 7.056 s off the head of the serial queue, and a fully capped runaway no
     longer breaks the RTF gate either (0.431 < 1, against the runaway's 3.277).
  => control untruncated (49 tokens against a cap of 286) with a parseable transcript, so
     the cap does not bite ordinary speech on this span either.

THE REPRODUCTION IS F1'S OWN FAILURE, WITHIN 4%, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT EVIDENCE.
  F1's runaways: 2024 / 2019 tokens, 8.49 / 8.29 s, RTF 3.398 / 3.318.
  Condition A:   2048        tokens, 8.129 s,        RTF 3.277.
  Measured generation rate 251.9 tok/s against the 238 tok/s iteration 16 derived from
  F1's own spans - which predicted ~1.2 s for a capped span where 1.074 s was measured.
  ITERATION 16'S PREDICTION WAS RIGHT, and is now a measurement rather than an argument.

THE QUEUE ARGUMENT, which is how this reaches F1's p95 without measuring the queue.
  F1 committed 42 spans over 73.3 s of speech = 1.745 s mean span arrival. An 8.129 s
  decode is 4.66x that interval and therefore MUST accumulate backlog - F1 measured
  exactly that, spans behind the runaways committing 4.9-8.3 s late. A 1.074 s decode is
  BELOW the arrival interval and therefore CANNOT accumulate any. That is structural, not
  an extrapolation, and it is the strongest statement available without the Mac.

WHAT THIS RUN DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated so the numbers are not borrowed:
 (a) THE RATE of runaways is unmeasured. The trigger is deliberate. This says nothing
     about how often a real meeting hits one - F1 saw 2 in 42 spans, iteration 23 saw 0
     in 58, and only F1/F3 can settle it.
 (b) THE TRIGGER IS temperature=2.0, i.e. high-entropy sampling, NOT a natural repeat
     loop. The shape of the degeneracy differs from F1's; the quantity under test - wall
     clock as a function of the token bound - does not.
 (c) D-C'S "A CAPPED SPAN COMMITS ITS WORDS" HALF IS NOT VERIFIED HERE. This trigger's
     output is unparseable at ANY length, so the product reported 0 tokens and an empty
     transcript for the capped AND the uncapped runs alike - there were no words to commit
     either way. F1's repeat loops were parseable fragments, so that half still rests on
     the unit tests alone. What the empty answers do show is H1's path firing three more
     times without going terminal.
 (d) The end-to-end user-visible p95 is a Mac-side number and is untouched by this.

THE TRIGGER HAD TO BE MEASURED AND THE FIRST TWO GUESSES WERE WRONG.
The endpoint's own /openapi.json has NO ignore_eos and NO min_tokens (25 properties read
off it), so the loop must come from a sampling field. Surveyed at the pre-D-c bound on the
same span, control 49 tokens:
  temperature=2.0        -> 2048  RUNS AWAY   <- the only candidate that works

  repetition_penalty=1.05                     -> 49, unchanged
A probe that had assumed repetition_penalty<1 induces loops - which is what the first
version of this probe's own docstring asserted - would have compared two identical empty

THE QUESTION. D-c ruled "cap the decode, commit what came back, never abandon the
span" and the ruling has two halves. Iteration 24 measured the first (8.129 s at the
pre-D-c 2048 bound vs 1.074 s at the deployed 286) and recorded that it could not
measure the second: its temperature=2.0 trigger produced output unparseable at ANY
length, so the capped and the uncapped run both committed empty and there were no
words either way. The risk that left open is specific and no gate sees it: a cap
truncates mid-fragment, and if that breaks the parse the span commits EMPTY - which
removes accepted audio's words from the transcript, i.e. exactly the loss D-c chose
capping over abandonment to avoid.

WHY IT IS MEASURABLE WITH NO MAC AND WITHOUT RE-RUNNING THE ENGINE. The live decode
is greedy - VllmRunner._build_fields sends temperature 0.0 unless the caller asks for
decoding="sample", and the live path never does - so the token sequence produced
under a cap of N is the N-token PREFIX of the sequence produced under 2048. The cap
decides when generation stops, not what it generates. So the transcript a capped
decode would have returned is
    detokenize(tokenize(<the recorded uncapped transcript>)[:cap])
computed with the DEPLOYED decoder's own tokenizer.

AND THE LICENCE IS VERIFIED, NOT ARGUED. Re-tokenising F1's two committed runaway
transcripts on the host returns 2024 and 2019 tokens - EXACTLY the generated-token
counts F1's own decode reported for those spans (context.md has had those two
numbers on record since iteration 16) - and re-tokenising each truncation returns
the same first 286 ids (round_trips true, both spans). A reconstruction that
reproduces the engine's own counter to the token is the reconstruction.

THE MEASUREMENT, on the deployed 77e0014, service venv python, product imported from
the deployed checkout:

LIMITS, stated so the numbers are not borrowed:

 (b) `capped`/`token_cap` are set by the stub. Harmless: the coordinator only
     forwards them to the canonical_processed event and never classifies on them.

THE DEFECT, AND IT IS FATAL TO THE RUN IT GUARDS. The per-minute loop asked

    case "$snaplast" in
      *terminal*|*failed*) ABORT="...session snapshot reports terminal/failed" ;;
    esac

but every HEALTHY snapshot body carries the literal KEY `terminal_failure`, and every
lane carries `failed_samples`. The glob therefore matched unconditionally, so the
16-minute soak would have printed "ABORT at +60s: session snapshot reports
terminal/failed" and stopped at minute 1 - reporting a dead meeting that was in perfect
health. A SUBSTRING TEST OVER A JSON DOCUMENT TESTS THE SCHEMA, NOT THE STATE.
`bash -n` passes on it. Nothing else in the loop would have caught it before the run.

THE INSTRUMENT. `soak-abort-probe.py` does not restate the driver's logic - it EXTRACTS
the shipped bytes between `# >>> soak-abort-decision` / `# <<< soak-abort-decision`
and the shipped `SNAP_PRUNE` jq filter, writes them into a bash harness, and runs them
against every body a real run recorded. It refuses (exit 2) if the markers or the filter
are missing, so a refactor cannot make it vacuously green. It auto-detects whether the
region is a function (`abort_reason`) or the legacy statement block that sets `$ABORT`,
which is what let the same instrument measure both sides.

THE CORPUS IS F1's OWN EVIDENCE DIRECTORY, and it already contained both sides of the
ruling - no synthesis needed for the interesting cases:
  54 polls  healthy            (terminal_failure null, v2 active, both lanes active)
   2 polls  lane-fault         (lanes failed,active - F1's real system-lane overrun,
                                session still active, terminal_failure still null)
  28 status status-running
   1 status status-lane-fault  (line 29: running:true, system failed/macos_buffer_overrun)
   1 status status-stopped     (line 30: F1's real POST-STOP status, running:false)
   4 controls synthesised by mutating a real body (terminal_failure set; v2 status
     terminal; three 401 rows in the snapshot.tsv tail - F3's own death shape)

RED / GREEN, both measured with the SAME instrument (the red run is HEAD's file plus
the two marker COMMENTS, nothing else - `git diff` on that step was 2 insertions, both
comment lines):

  class               n   RED aborted/wrong   GREEN aborted/wrong
  healthy            54       54 / 54              0 / 0
  lane-fault          2        2 /  2              0 / 0
  status-running     28       28 / 28              0 / 0
  status-lane-fault   1        1 /  1              0 / 0
  status-stopped      1        1 /  0              1 / 0
  control-dead        4        4 /  0 (vacuous)    4 / 0
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  VERDICT           90     FAIL 85 wrong        PASS 90/90, rc=0

The four control-dead rows "passed" in the RED run only because the same unconditional
glob fires on everything; their red reason string is the healthy one. The RED status-
stopped row also exposes the block's second bug, `ABORT="${ABORT:-}session..."`, which
concatenates: "client reports running=falsesession snapshot reports terminal/failed".

THE RULING, recorded because it is a decision and not a repair. Abort a soak only on a
session that GENUINELY CANNOT CONTINUE - the same rule the third and fifth amendments
settled for the product:
  * client `running: false`                     -> the capture is gone
  * `snapshot.terminal_failure` non-null        -> the server ended the meeting
  * `v2_session.status` != "active"             -> likewise, with its reason
  * three consecutive refused snapshot polls    -> F3's own death shape; once the
    session is released the view routes 401 and the body carries no state to read
A LANE FAULT IS RECORDED AND NEVER ABORTS. Phase M's governing rule is that a fault on
one lane must not end the meeting, so a driver that stopped there would destroy the one
piece of evidence 53/48/49/D-a exist to produce. The lane timeline goes to
live-canary-clauses.py section 8, which already decides it.

THE PROBE FOUND A DEFECT IN ITS OWN FIX, which is the strongest argument for keeping it.
The first repair read the client state as `jq -r '.running // empty'`. JQ'S ALTERNATIVE
OPERATOR TREATS `false` ITSELF AS AN ABSENT VALUE, so that form silently swallows
exactly the case the line exists to catch: `ctl-client-running-false` came back
"continue" and the run was 89/90, not 90/90. Now
`try (if .running == false then "false" else empty end) catch empty`.

SECOND FIX, SAME CLASS, BOTH DRIVERS. `snapshot.tsv`, `events.tsv` and `status.tsv` are
written by the nohup'd pollers with `>>` and were never truncated at the start of a run.
A soak or canary is RETRIED - iteration 21's attempt died in setup - and a second run
into the same $OUT would silently concatenate two meetings, so the reducer's "version is
monotone" and "first non-200" clauses would read across the seam and answer about no run
that happened. Both drivers now truncate every appended file (and the soak removes stale
snap-full-*.json), and say out loud how many lines they truncated - because an orphaned
poller from the previous attempt keeps appending regardless and that is visible only to
an operator who knows to look.

VALIDATION (smallest commands that produced real evidence):
  python3 scripts/ralph-afk/soak-abort-probe.py --script /tmp/i26-soak-HEAD-marked.sh
      -> FAIL, 85/90 wrong, 54/54 healthy polls abort   (/tmp/i26-abort-red.json)
  python3 scripts/ralph-afk/soak-abort-probe.py
      -> PASS, 90/90, rc=0                              (/tmp/i26-abort-green.json)
  bash -n scripts/ralph-afk/live-soak.sh                -> OK
  bash -n scripts/ralph-afk/live-canary.sh              -> OK
Evidence: /tmp/i26-abort-red.json, /tmp/i26-abort-red.txt, /tmp/i26-abort-green.json,
  /tmp/i26-abort-green.txt, /tmp/i26-soak-HEAD-marked.sh.

Learned.
(1) AN INSTRUMENT THAT HAS NEVER RUN IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT IT WORKS, and `bash -n`
    measures nothing about a decision. The soak driver was carefully written, reviewed
    in its own iteration, and would have destroyed the run it exists to produce.
(2) A SUBSTRING TEST OVER A STRUCTURED DOCUMENT TESTS THE SCHEMA, NOT THE STATE. Every
    field name the state might use is present on every healthy poll.
(3) THE RECORDED EVIDENCE OF AN EARLIER RUN IS THE BEST CORPUS FOR THE NEXT RUN'S
    INSTRUMENT. F1's directory supplied a real healthy meeting, a real lane fault on
    both the server and the client side, and a real post-stop status line - four of the
    six classes this probe needed, with no synthesis and no host.
(4) A FIX DESERVES THE SAME INSTRUMENT AS THE DEFECT. The jq `//` trap was invisible to
    reading and obvious to the probe, one minute after the probe existed.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP - the strongest remaining un-mirrored property.
live_snapshot and live_events are sync `def` handlers (live_transport.py:285,307)
so Starlette runs them in its threadpool, while accept_live_frame is `async def`
and runs on the event loop. On the Mac TWO view readers poll concurrently - the
app's own latency probe and the portal poller - while frames are being posted.
This probe is single-threaded and strictly serial, so it structurally cannot
overlap a read with a write. Give it a background reader thread (two, to match)
and re-run before designing anything.

THE MECHANISM, ONE LINE, AND THE PRODUCT ALREADY CONTAINS ITS OWN FIX.
  vllm_runner.py:111   elapsed_sec = time.time() - started        <- WALL clock
  live_adapters.py:305 started = time.monotonic()                 <- taken...
  live_adapters.py:317 elapsed_sec = time.monotonic() - started   <- ...and used
                       ONLY on the empty-transcript branch
  live_adapters.py:344 elapsed_sec = _runner_elapsed_sec(result)  <- the success
                       branch throws the monotonic measurement away and takes the
                       runner's wall-clock number
  live_adapters.py:508-527 _finite_non_negative_float rejects a negative one as a
                       NON-RETRYABLE LiveProviderError
  live_service_runtime.py:733 _process_in_flight_item -> _fail -> terminal
  live_transport.py:87-101 -> live_auth.py:377-385  every view route 401
  live_service_runtime.py:462 _raise_terminal        every frame 409
  One cause, both symptoms, no lane and no lease - as iteration 26 deduced.

VALIDATION 3 - and the wall clock on ga0-alienware-rtx4070ti IS NOT MONOTONE.
90 s of paired time.time()/time.monotonic() sampling at 20 ms on the host
(/tmp/i28-clock.txt): 4297 samples, THREE backward steps of -1.523536,
-1.504152 and -1.502687 s at monotonic 1731399.207 / 1731431.460 / 1731463.740 -
intervals of 32.25 s and 32.28 s. A ~1.5 s STEP BACKWARDS EVERY ~32.3 s, on a
host whose timedatectl reports "System clock synchronized: yes / NTP service:
active". This is WSL2 being resynchronised. It is a HOST fact, not a code fact -
but a meeting must not end because NTP corrected a clock.

WHY THE DEATH TIME LOOKED RANDOM, AND WHY TWO PROBE RUNS SURVIVED. A decode
brackets ~0.33 s of wall time and a span freezes every 2.5 s, so a decode is in
flight ~13% of the time; one step per 32.3 s therefore kills a session with ~13%
probability per step. F1 run A died at t+18.1 s, run B at t+32.1 s, this run at
t+31.5 s; iteration 23's 120 s run and iteration 27's 150 s run survived. That is
exactly the distribution a periodic EXTERNAL event sampled by a 13% duty cycle
produces - and it is why five straight audio hypotheses came back clean.

THE CLASS, FOR THE FIFTH TIME. A decoder whose TIMING METADATA is untrustworthy
still returned a transcript. The span is fine; only the number used for RTF is
not. J3's LiveProviderTransientError already exists for "the decoder blinked" and
degrades one span - this condition is strictly less serious and is terminal.

A SECOND CONSEQUENCE THAT TOUCHES A PRD CLAUSE. elapsed_sec is the numerator of
"decoder p95 RTF < 1". Every RTF this project has recorded came off a clock that
steps 1.5 s backwards every 32 s, so any decode bracketing a step is wrong by
~1.5 s in one direction or the other. Surviving spans are unaffected only because
a NEGATIVE one kills the run before it can be reported. F1's two 8.5 s runaways
are NOT clock artifacts: 1.5 s is far too small, and both were corroborated by
2024 and 2019 generated tokens from the deployed tokenizer.

HOST CLEAN, checked after (/tmp/i28-host-after.txt against /tmp/i28-host-baseline
.txt): HEAD 77e0014, git status clean; moss-live-web 350731 / moss-web 301112 /
moss-vllm 322117 all NRestarts=0 and unmoved since iteration 20; live-runs 0
entries; no /tmp/mtd-live-*; 0 journal tracebacks; 0 `live helper terminal` lines;
batch 200; device store 12 devices / 1 unrevoked (m4mbp's AB600574..., this run's

Learned.
(1) THE RECORDED NEXT STEP WAS RIGHT FOR THE WRONG REASON. Concurrent readers
    reproduced it, but a reader takes the runtime lock and mutates nothing, and a
    13%-per-step hazard reproduces on its own eventually. Honest verdict: the
    readers are probably NOT load-bearing; what they bought was the timestamp -
    both readers 401 within 2 ms of each other and 200 ms before the frame 409,
    which is what pins the cut to one instant and one cause.
(2) FIVE HYPOTHESES ABOUT THE AUDIO FAILED BECAUSE THE CAUSE WAS NOT IN THE
    AUDIO. Iterations 26 and 27 tested lane voicing, span density, identity,
    lease arithmetic and lane drift. The trigger was an external periodic event
    on the host. When a family of hypotheses all come back clean, the next
    question is not "which one did I model wrong" but "is the cause even in the
    thing I am varying".
(3) A WALL CLOCK IS NOT A DURATION. The product measures the same quantity two
    ways, twelve lines apart, and uses the wrong one on the branch that matters.
    Anything that subtracts two time.time() readings and treats the result as a
    duration is a latent terminal failure on any host that runs NTP.
(4) THE PROBE THAT COST NOTHING PAID FOR ITSELF TWICE OVER. view-reader-probe.py
    took ten minutes and caught a crash that would have burned the pairing code
    AND the iteration. Iteration 26 paid that bill; this one did not.

source under the post-merge freeze, in moss_transcribe_diarize/. Recommended
scope for that authorization, all inside moss_transcribe_diarize/ and tests/:
  (a) measure the live decode's elapsed on time.monotonic() - transcribe_pcm
      ALREADY takes it at live_adapters.py:305 and uses it at :317; the success
      branch at :344 need only stop discarding it;
  (b) rule, once, that untrustworthy timing metadata degrades (elapsed/RTF null,
      recorded on canonical_processed) rather than ending the meeting - the third
      amendment's governing rule applied to the fifth instance of its class;
  (c) a real-seam regression in tests/test_live_pipeline_seams.py driving the
      coordinator with a runner whose result carries a NEGATIVE elapsed_sec, red
      before and green after;
  (d) note that this also repairs the PRD's decoder-RTF clause, which is measured
      from this number.
Until it lands, F1 and F3 will keep dying at ~13% per 32 s - so do NOT re-run
